description:
## Outcome

`mikehostetler/homebrew-tap` contains a `jido-cli` formula that installs the correct isolated macOS or Linux artifact and tests `jido --version`. Release automation can open a narrow formula-update pull request.

## Work

1. Add target selectors for macOS ARM64, macOS x86-64, and Linux x86-64 archives.
2. Use immutable GitHub release URLs and exact SHA-256 values.
3. Install the packaged `jido` command without a Homebrew Erlang or Elixir dependency.
4. Add a non-interactive formula test for version and basic help.
5. Add update automation that changes version, URLs, and checksums in a pull request.
6. Use a GitHub App or token limited to the tap repository.
7. Document install, upgrade, uninstall, state preservation, and unsigned candidate limits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `brew install mikehostetler/tap/jido-cli` selects the correct artifact.
- [ ] `brew deps jido-cli` does not add Erlang.
- [ ] The formula test runs the isolated command.
- [ ] A bad checksum or wrong target fails installation.
- [ ] Update automation opens a reviewable pull request and never pushes directly to the tap default branch.
- [ ] The formula has no service definition in this task.

## Tests

Run formula audit and install tests on supported macOS and Linux runners, including upgrade from one fixture version.

## Non-goals

Do not submit to `homebrew/core` or start a daemon during installation.
title: Add Homebrew installation and tap update automation without a service
